summary: This project is a digital platform that documents and explores the historical and scientific objects left behind by space missions on the Moon and Mars. It addresses the lack of awareness about space debris by transforming it into technological relics, active scientific instruments, and testaments to our humanity. Ultimately, it helps people connect with space exploration in a closer, more visual, and emotional way.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

We created an interactive website featuring space-themed games designed for children to discover the history of the objects left behind on the Moon and Mars while having fun. Through engaging challenges and exploration, kids learn the fascinating stories behind everything from Alan Shepard’s golf balls to historic landers and forgotten robots.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Instead of seeing space exploration as distant or overly technical, our platform transforms space debris and abandoned hardware into exciting stories of human curiosity and achievement. Its main benefit is making STEM and space history accessible, visual, and emotionally engaging for young learners—sparking their imagination and inspiring the next generation of explorers.

Tools, Software & Data Used

  • Design & Web Development: We used Canva to design and build the website, allowing us to create a visually appealing, colorful, and intuitive environment tailored specifically for children.
  • Research & Content: All historical facts and mission details were researched directly from the official NASA website and supplemented with Wikipedia, ensuring scientific and historical accuracy adapted into a simple, fun narrative.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Our project stands out creatively by turning real planetary archaeology into gamified storytelling—blending playful challenges with true historical artifacts. When developing the platform, our team carefully considered:

  • Age-Appropriate Simplicity: Translating complex aerospace data into clear, captivating stories that children can easily understand.
  • User Experience (UX): Designing bright visuals and straightforward navigation so kids can explore independently.
  • Factual Accuracy: Verifying every object’s story with official space agency sources before adapting it into a game.
